anomalies.observed: T3 is a P-channel AON6407 connected as a high-side device between the fused input and the bulk 24 V rail (pin 2/S on /+24V_F, pin 3/D on +24V, pin 1/G on /G_RPP). It is not connected to the ATO_VALVE control net. The ATO valve load is driven by T5 (AO3400A) on /D_ATO, while ATO_VALVE only connects M1 pin J1_12 and R10.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that T3 is the ATO solenoid-valve low-side N-MOSFET switch driving the ATO_VALVE net, with its gate driven through R10 and pre-driven by T4. If T3 is instead intended as a reverse-polarity-protection P-MOSFET (as the /G_RPP net suggests), standard practice would place the P-MOSFET source on the protected rail and drain on the fused input side so the body diode blocks reverse/backfeed; here the source is on the fused input side.

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).

anomalies.impact: The specified valve driver reference is not connected to the valve; the valve is instead driven by T5. Additionally, the 24 V input path contains a high-side P-MOSFET network whose source/drain orientation does not match a conventional reverse-polarity/ideal-diode P-MOSFET arrangement, potentially leaving reverse-polarity or backfeed protection ineffective.

parsed.summary: The netlist contradicts the specified role of T3: it is not the ATO-valve low-side switch but a P-channel MOSFET connected in the 24 V input path, while T5 drives the valve. This reference/role mismatch is not listed among the known limitations and suggests an anomaly in the build.
